rows.verbatim:
The Contractor shall be responsible for the overall performance of the contract and provide all necessary resources to
meet contract requirements.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall be responsible for overall contract performance and provide all necessary resources to meet requirements.

rows.verbatim: All work completed under this contract shall comply with contract requirements.
rows.normalized: All work completed under the contract shall comply with contract requirements.

rows.verbatim:
All
deliverables under this contract shall not be marked proprietary or confidential or with any other markings limiting
the Government’s use, unless otherwise specified by the Government.
rows.normalized: Deliverables shall not be marked proprietary/confidential or otherwise restrict Government use, unless the Government specifies otherwise.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor shall provide services globally without exception.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall provide services globally without exception.

rows.verbatim:
In the event that the Contractor cannot provide a
medevac in specific parts of the world, then the Contractor shall provide sufficient rationale to the NASA COR why
it cannot and provide an alternate solution at no additional cost beyond the prepaid amount.
rows.normalized: If the Contractor cannot provide medevac in a region, it shall provide rationale to the NASA COR and propose an alternate solution at no additional cost.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor shall be responsible for all medevac and medical travel service costs.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall be responsible for all medevac and medical travel service costs.

rows.verbatim:
The Contractor shall ensure that any of the contractor’s owned, leased, or chartered aircraft used in the performance
of this contract comply with all applicable local and long‑distance aircraft and pilot requirements, including those
applicable to both prime contractors and subcontractors.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall ensure all owned/leased/chartered aircraft comply with applicable aircraft and pilot requirements, including for subcontractors.

rows.verbatim:
Aircraft used for NASA traveler transportation shall be certificated, operated, and maintained in accordance with the
requirements of 14 CFR:
a. Part 21—Certification Procedures for Products and Parts
b. Part 25—Airworthiness Standards: Transport Category Airplanes Part 29—Airworthiness Standards:
Transport Category Rotorcraft Part 39—Airworthiness Directives
c. Part 43—Maintenance, Preventative Maintenance, Rebuilding, and Alteration Part 61—Certification: Pilots,
Flight Instructors, and Ground Instructors
d. Part 65—Certification: Airmen Other Than Flight Crewmembers Part 91—General Operating and Flight Rules
e. Part 135—Operating Requirements: Commuter and On-Demand Operations
rows.normalized: Aircraft used for NASA traveler transport shall be certificated, operated, and maintained per listed 14 CFR parts; 5 lettered items in total.

rows.verbatim:
The Contractor shall have a documented Safety Management System (SMS) in accordance with International Civil
Aviation Organization (ICAO), Federal, and industry standards. Requirements include the following:
a. A structured means of safety risk management decision making.
b. A means of demonstrating safety management capability before system failures occur.
c. Increased confidence in risk controls through structured safety assurance processes.
d. An effective interface for knowledge sharing.
e. A safety promotion framework to support a sound safety culture.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall maintain a documented SMS per ICAO/Federal/industry standards, including 5 listed requirements.

rows.verbatim:
The Contractor shall indemnify the Government for any occurrence, action, or claim that might trigger the
Government's liability; unless the Government is found to be liable.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall indemnify the Government for claims triggering Government liability, unless the Government is found liable.

rows.verbatim:
The rights and obligations of the parties under
this clause shall survive the termination, expiration, or completion of this contract.
rows.normalized: Rights and obligations under this clause shall survive contract termination/expiration/completion.
Contractor shall provide medical travel services worldwide, including 14 listed services (a-n).

rows.verbatim:
The Contractor shall transport the injured or ill traveler to nearest appropriate medical facility that practices U.S.
standards of medical care.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall transport injured/ill traveler to nearest facility meeting U.S. standards of medical care.

rows.verbatim:
In the event that the medical facility does not meet the U.S. standards of medical care, the Contractor shall
provide sufficient rationale to the NASA/JSC Chief Medical Officer and NASA Contracting Officer
Representative (COR) for using the proposed facility.
rows.normalized: If the medical facility does not meet U.S. standards, Contractor shall provide rationale to NASA/JSC CMO and COR.

rows.verbatim:
The Contractor shall co-develop with NASA the notification process for timely communication, integration and
operational protocols with NASA physicians, and dissemination of confidential medical reports.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall co-develop with NASA the notification process for communication, integration, protocols, and dissemination of medical reports.

rows.verbatim:
The Contractor shall obtain all necessary insurance information from the traveler, as required, and shall coordinate
the payment of personal medical expenses incurred by the traveler that are not arranged for or provided directly by
the Contractor.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall obtain insurance info from traveler and coordinate payment of personal medical expenses not arranged by Contractor.

rows.verbatim:
Such coordination shall be conducted exclusively between the Contractor, the traveler, and the
traveler’s insurer, without any involvement from the Government.
rows.normalized: Such coordination shall occur exclusively between Contractor, traveler, and insurer, without Government involvement.

rows.verbatim:
The Contractor shall provide group membership as specified in Section B Firm Fixed Price (FFP) Group
Membership.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall provide group membership per Section B FFP Group Membership.

rows.verbatim:
The Contractor shall provide an “Air Ambulance Medical Evacuation” (medevac) service in response to a
worldwide medical emergency for NASA’s Human Spaceflight Mission Directorate (HSMD), Johnson Space
Center (JSC), or other travelers identified by NASA (referred to as ‘traveler(s)’ throughout) on a pre-paid basis
regardless of traveler’s home location or country of origin.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall provide Air Ambulance Medical Evacuation service worldwide for NASA-identified travelers on a pre-paid basis.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor shall provide transportation for three accompanying travelers specified by NASA on the same transport as the injured/ill individual requiring a medevac.
rows.normalized: Contractor must provide transportation for three NASA-specified accompanying travelers on the same medevac transport as the injured/ill individual.

rows.verbatim: In the event that the same transport cannot accommodate all three accompanying travelers, at least one accompanying traveler specified by NASA shall be accommodated on the same transport.
rows.normalized: If the same transport cannot accommodate all three accompanying travelers, Contractor must accommodate at least one NASA-specified accompanying traveler on the same transport.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor shall provide sufficient rationale to the NASA Contracting Officer Representative (COR) why it cannot transport all accompanying travelers and provide alternate transportation for the remaining accompanying travelers within 24 hours to the same location as the injured or ill traveler.
rows.normalized: Contractor must provide rationale to COR when unable to transport all accompanying travelers and must provide alternate transportation for remaining travelers within 24 hours to the same location.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor provided services shall meet the Commission on Accreditation Medical Transport Services (CAMTS), National Accreditation Alliance of Medical Transport Applications (NAAMTA) Global, and European Aero-Medical Institute (EURAMI) accreditation standards or equivalent for personnel and assets.
rows.normalized: Contractor-provided services must meet CAMTS, NAAMTA Global, and EURAMI accreditation standards or equivalent for personnel and assets.

rows.verbatim: Active credentials must be maintained according to the standard renewal timelines dictated by the respective accrediting body.
rows.normalized: Contractor must maintain active credentials per the accrediting body's standard renewal timelines.

rows.verbatim: Any deviations must be reported to the JSC Chief Medical Officer and Contracting Officer Representative (COR), and approved by NASA prior to implementation, unless otherwise specified by the Contracting Officer.
rows.normalized: Contractor must report any accreditation deviations to the JSC Chief Medical Officer and COR and obtain NASA approval prior to implementation, unless the Contracting Officer specifies otherwise.

rows.verbatim: The decision to perform a medevac shall be made jointly (50/50) by NASA and the Contractor, who will apply U.S. standards of medical care.
rows.normalized: The decision to perform a medevac must be made jointly by NASA and the Contractor, applying U.S. standards of medical care.

rows.verbatim: This independent third party will be mutually agreed upon within 30 calendar days of contract award.
rows.normalized: NASA and Contractor must mutually agree on the independent third party within 30 calendar days of contract award.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor shall provide a medical evacuation using a Portable Medical Isolation Unit (e.g. infectious disease) upon request by NASA.
rows.normalized: Contractor must provide a medical evacuation using a Portable Medical Isolation Unit upon NASA's request.

rows.verbatim: If a medical event occurs, all costs for evacuation and additional medical travel services shall be the responsibility of the Contractor and no additional cost beyond the prepaid provided group membership as specified in Section B Firm Fixed Price (FFP) Group Membership amount will be incurred by NASA or its travelers.
rows.normalized: If a medical event occurs, Contractor is responsible for all evacuation and additional medical travel service costs beyond the prepaid FFP group membership amount.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor shall conduct a program status meeting each contract year with NASA management and JSC's Chief Medical Officer, with the first meeting happening within 90 calendar days of the start of the contract.
rows.normalized: Contractor must conduct a program status meeting each contract year with NASA management and JSC's Chief Medical Officer, first meeting within 90 days of contract start.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor shall participate in NASA Contingency Tabletop simulations of evacuation events to validate communication and operations plans and decision-making procedures (estimate twice per year).
rows.normalized: Contractor must participate in NASA Contingency Tabletop simulations of evacuation events, approximately twice per year.

rows.verbatim:
The Contractor shall establish and provide, within 60 calendar days of contract start and maintain for the duration
of the contract, the GOP advance service agreements with the specific medical facilities that NASA identifies as
critical medical facilities in Russia and Kazakhstan.
rows.normalized: Contractor must establish and maintain, within 60 days of contract start and for the duration of the contract, GOP advance service agreements with NASA-identified critical medical facilities in Russia and Kazakhstan.

rows.verbatim: If the Contractor cannot establish a GOP advance service agreement at one of NASA’s identified medical facilities in Russia/Kazakhstan by the end of that 60-day period, then the Contractor shall notify the NASA COR and provide an alternate course of action to meet the intent of the GOP advance service agreement.
rows.normalized: If Contractor cannot establish a GOP advance service agreement within 60 days, it must notify the NASA COR and provide an alternate course of action.

rows.verbatim: Annually by December 15th, the Contractor shall provide a written summary report on the status of GOP advance service agreements for the NASA identified hospitals.
rows.normalized: Contractor must provide a written summary report on GOP advance service agreement status by December 15th annually.

rows.verbatim:
The Contractor shall establish and provide, within 60 calendar days of contract start and updated annually for
currency by Oct 1st, a written medevac plan of action/response for each location that NASA frequently visits to
include Moscow, Russia; Baikonur, Kazakhstan; Karaganda, Kazakhstan; Nordwijk, Netherlands; Montreal,
Canada; Tsukuba, Japan; and Tanegashima, Japan. The plan shall include at a minimum:
a. Specific points of contact the Contractor will utilize to access restricted airports or facilities;
b. Unique country and local specific requirements for medevac services and plans on how to address each;
c. Specific facilities, capabilities, and transport services in country the Contractor will utilize for bed-to-bed
medical transport including any operational limitations or risk factors;
d. Transport and Access Considerations, including typical timelines and constraints for access to airports, border
crossings, restricted areas, or local authorities.
e. Regional Risk Assessment, summarizing relevant geopolitical, infrastructure, transportation, or environmental
risks, along with proposed mitigation strategies.
f. Whether selected medical providers accept U.S Government employee medical insurance plans;
g. List of data and documentation the Contractor requires NASA to provide to support medevac.
h. Verification and Validation Procedures, describing how the Contractor annually confirms the accuracy of
facility information, capabilities, and points of contact data.
rows.normalized: Contractor must establish, within 60 days of contract start (updated annually by Oct 1), a written medevac plan of action/response for each of 7 named locations, containing at minimum 8 elements: points of contact, country-specific requirements, transport capabilities, access considerations, risk assessment, insurance acceptance, required NASA data, and verification procedures.

rows.verbatim:
The Contractor shall provide, within 10 calendar days of contract start, a secure electronic registration capability
that:
a. Provides travelers with a description of the scope of Contractor’s services in accordance with this SOW.
b. Educates travelers on specific instructions to follow should a medical incident or emergency occur and
traveler’s responsibilities in accordance with this SOW.
c. Captures critical information from travelers that expedites medical assistance and evacuation when
necessary.
d. Meets industry standards for data protection, accessibility, storage, and retention requirements of private
medical and personal information (e.g. Personally Identifiable Information, Health Insurance, etc.).
rows.normalized: Contractor must provide, within 10 days of contract start, a secure electronic registration capability meeting 4 requirements: describes service scope, educates travelers on procedures/responsibilities, captures critical traveler information, and meets data protection/retention standards.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor shall provide a weekly report on current and historical NASA traveler enrollment and critical traveler information.
rows.normalized: Contractor must provide a weekly report on NASA traveler enrollment and critical traveler information.

rows.verbatim:
The Contractor shall provide, by Sept 30th annually, a summary report of all medical incidents by date and
incidence level (Levels 1-4), medical evacuations, reservations and call-ups of medical transport via air
ambulance for Soyuz landings (if executed) supported by the Contractor during that year.
rows.normalized: Contractor must provide, by Sept 30th annually, a summary report of medical incidents, evacuations, and Soyuz-related transport reservations/call-ups for that year.

rows.verbatim:
The Contractor shall provide, within 60 calendar days after contract award, wallet sized cards to the NASA COR
for every NASA traveler with information including an international call number for support for medical support
and emergencies.
rows.normalized: Contractor must provide wallet-sized cards with an international call number to the NASA COR for every NASA traveler within 60 days after contract award.

rows.verbatim: Approximately 1,200 cards are required annually for NASA travelers.
rows.normalized: Contractor must produce approximately 1,200 wallet cards annually for NASA travelers.

rows.verbatim: The cards shall be updated for currency and provided annually thereafter to the NASA COR by Oct 1st.
rows.normalized: Contractor must update and provide the wallet cards annually to the NASA COR by Oct 1st.

rows.verbatim:
The Contractor shall provide a Reservation and Call-up/Execution service for medical transport via air ambulance
for Soyuz crew landing event.
rows.normalized: Contractor must provide a Reservation and Call-up/Execution service for medical transport via air ambulance for Soyuz crew landing events.

rows.verbatim:
Within 36 hours of NASA reservation, the Contractor shall provide a Reservation Readiness Package consisting of a dedicated tail-number assignment, overflight and landing permits,
diplomatic route clearances, aircraft medical and transport capabilities, and staffing plan.
rows.normalized: Within 36 hours of NASA's reservation, Contractor must provide a Reservation Readiness Package consisting of tail-number assignment, overflight/landing permits, diplomatic route clearances, aircraft medical/transport capabilities, and staffing plan.

rows.verbatim: NASA will provide call-up/execute notification to the Contractor no later than 36 hours prior to the Soyuz landing event.
rows.normalized: NASA will notify the Contractor of call-up/execution no later than 36 hours prior to Soyuz landing, establishing the Contractor's response deadline.

rows.verbatim: The crew member and the associated NASA flight surgeon shall be transported to Houston, Texas.
rows.normalized: Contractor must transport the crew member and associated NASA flight surgeon to Houston, Texas.

rows.verbatim:
Within 3 hours of the NASA call-up, the Contractor shall activate the asset and personnel and provide an
Operational Deployment Package consisting of a copy of the officially filed International Civil Aviation
Organization (ICAO) flight plan, crew-rest compliance, real-time satellite tracking link, confirmation of NASA
passengers on flight manifest, finalized staffing plan, and communications matrix.
rows.normalized: Within 3 hours of NASA call-up, Contractor must activate asset/personnel and provide an Operational Deployment Package with ICAO flight plan, crew-rest compliance, satellite tracking link, passenger manifest confirmation, staffing plan, and communications matrix.

rows.verbatim:
If a reservation or call-up for medical transport via air ambulance occurs, all costs for the reservation and medical
transport via air ambulance shall be the responsibility of the Contractor and no additional cost beyond the prepaid
reservation fee and call-up fee as specified in Section B Firm Fixed Price (FFP) Group Membership amount will
be incurred by NASA or its travelers.
rows.normalized: If a reservation or call-up occurs, Contractor is responsible for all reservation and transport costs beyond the prepaid FFP fees.

rows.verbatim: Describe the offeror’s approach, teaming arrangements, resources, processes and procedures to provide worldwide medical evacuation and medical travel services capabilities per the requirements of the Statement of Work (SOW).
rows.normalized: Offeror shall describe its approach, teaming, resources, processes and procedures to provide worldwide medevac/travel services per the SOW.

rows.verbatim: The Offeror shall explain its capabilities and expected operational timelines/durations with medical extractions for potential life or death circumstances with a point of origin in a non-western country similar in size, scope, and complexity to the requirements in the SOW and scenarios.

rows.normalized: Offeror shall explain capabilities/timelines for air ambulance reservation/call-up for Soyuz landing astronauts.

rows.verbatim: The Offeror shall provide a compliance matrix (cross-walk table) explicitly mapping each element of the Statement of Work (SOW) to the specific section and page number where it is addressed in the Technical Capability Proposal.
rows.normalized: Offeror shall provide a compliance matrix mapping each SOW element to its location in the Technical Capability Proposal.

rows.verbatim: For each SOW element, the table must point to a narrative explaining the Offeror's specific methodology and implementation approach; a restatement or acknowledgment of the requirement is insufficient for evaluation.
rows.normalized: For each SOW element, the compliance matrix must point to a narrative on methodology/implementation; mere restatement is insufficient.

rows.verbatim: Describe the air and ground transportation assets (type/design/age/capabilities/locations) your company uses to provide worldwide medical evacuations per the requirements of the Statement of Work (SOW).
rows.normalized: Offeror shall describe air/ground transportation assets used for worldwide medevac per the SOW.

rows.verbatim:
Provide evidence showing your company is capable of providing each of the following services:
1. Advanced airway management including ventilator support/oxygenation
2. Advanced medication management in flight (anti-seizure meds, IV meds, etc.)
3. Advanced Cardiac Life Support
4. Medical Escort Services
5. Medevac Using Portable Medical Isolation Unit (e.g. infectious disease medevac)
rows.normalized: Offeror shall provide evidence of capability for 5 listed medical services (airway mgmt, in-flight medication, ACLS, medical escort, isolation-unit medevac).

rows.verbatim: Describe how your company will apply US standards of medical care for travelers under this contract?
rows.normalized: Offeror shall describe how it will apply US standards of medical care for travelers.

rows.verbatim: Provide evidence that demonstrates how your quality assurance program ensures that only appropriately trained, certified, and credentialed medical staff, equipment and transports are used to provide services within your company’s limits.
rows.normalized: Offeror shall provide evidence of its QA program ensuring only appropriately trained/certified/credentialed staff, equipment, and transport are used.

rows.verbatim: Please provide similar evidence for any subcontractors.
rows.normalized: Offeror shall provide similar QA evidence for any subcontractors.

rows.verbatim: Additionally, please submit proof of CAMTS, NAAMTA Global and/or EURAMI certification or equivalent.
rows.normalized: Offeror shall submit proof of CAMTS, NAAMTA Global, and/or EURAMI certification or equivalent.

rows.verbatim: For equivalent certification, please provide narrative on applicability and a compliance mapping matrix alongside the technical proposal.
rows.normalized: If offering equivalent certification instead of CAMTS/NAAMTA/EURAMI, offeror shall provide a narrative on applicability and a compliance mapping matrix with the technical proposal.

rows.verbatim: Provide all steps required to execute a Contractor-provided medical evacuation under this contract.

rows.verbatim:
Technical Capability for each proposal will be evaluated as defined with the ratings as follows:
“Acceptable” (A) Rating – A proposal will be rated “Acceptable” under the Technical Capability Factor, where ALL Subfactors are individually rated acceptable based on the level of reasonableness, feasibility, and completeness, such that there are no associated risks that would jeopardize an acceptable level of contract performance.
“Unacceptable” (U) Rating – A proposal will be rated “Unacceptable” under the Technical Capability Factor, where ANY Subfactor is individually rated unacceptable based on the level of reasonableness, feasibility, and completeness, such that associated risks do jeopardize an acceptable level of contract performance.
“Potentially Acceptable” (PA) Rating – A proposal will be rated “Potentially Acceptable” under the Technical Capability Factor, when after the initial evaluation, the proposal does not fully meet the definition for an “Acceptable” or “Unacceptable” rating and the Government anticipates that additional information obtained during discussions could result in a proposal rating of “Acceptable”.
rows.normalized: Technical Capability will be rated Acceptable, Unacceptable, or Potentially Acceptable per the three defined criteria; 3 rating definitions in total.

rows.verbatim:
Technical Capability will be determined by review of information submitted by the Offeror to the following Sections:
1. Technical Capability Questions/Responses
2. Scenarios
rows.normalized: Technical Capability rating will be based on the Offeror's submitted Technical Capability Q&A and Scenarios sections.
